dialogue.speaker: Valentina
dialogue.spanish: ¡Aló, Pipe! ¿Dónde vienen? Llevamos media hora haciendo fila en la entrada del bar.
dialogue.english: Hello, Pipe! Where are you guys? We've been waiting in line at the bar entrance for half an hour.

dialogue.speaker: Pipe
dialogue.spanish: ¡Ay, qué pena con vos, Vale! Nos cogió un trancón horrible por la carrera Séptima.
dialogue.english: Oh, I'm so sorry, Vale! We got caught in a terrible traffic jam on Seventh Avenue.

slang.actualMeaning: a massive traffic jam / gridlock (Colombian Spanish)
slang.example: Salí temprano pero había un trancón monumental en la autopista.

dialogue.speaker: Valentina
dialogue.spanish: ¡No me digás! Bueno, apúrense que antes de las diez no cobran cover y la rumba está buenísima.
dialogue.english: Don't tell me that! Well, hurry up because before ten o'clock there's no cover charge and the party is awesome.

slang.actualMeaning: the party / night out dancing (standard in Colombia)
slang.example: Este viernes se armó la rumba en Chapinero.

dialogue.speaker: Pipe
dialogue.spanish: Ya nos bajamos del taxi a dos cuadras y vamos corriendo. ¡Guardanos puesto en la mesa!
dialogue.english: We just got out of the taxi two blocks away and we're running over. Save us a spot at the table!

questions.question: Why is Pipe running late to meet Valentina at the bar?
options: His taxi got stuck in a terrible traffic jam ('un trancón') on Seventh Avenue
He forgot his ID card at home
He went to the wrong neighborhood
questions.explanation: Pipe says: 'Nos cogió un trancón horrible por la carrera Séptima.'

questions.question: Why is it important that Pipe arrive before 10:00 PM?
options: There is no cover charge before 10:00 PM
Valentina has to leave at 10:00 PM
questions.explanation: Valentina says: 'antes de las diez no cobran cover y la rumba está buenísima.'

questions.question: What did Pipe and his friends do to get there faster?
options: They hopped out of the taxi two blocks away and are running the rest of the way
They asked the driver to take a shortcut
questions.explanation: Pipe says: 'Ya nos bajamos del taxi a dos cuadras y vamos corriendo.'

questions.question: Slang Side Quest: In Colombia, what do '¡Qué pena con vos!', 'un trancón', and 'la rumba' mean?
options: '¡Qué pena!' = I'm so sorry / excuse me; 'un trancón' = a traffic jam; 'la rumba' = the party / night out
'¡Qué pena!' = How sad; 'un trancón' = a big drink; 'la rumba' = the band
'¡Qué pena!' = How embarrassing; 'un trancón' = a rainstorm; 'la rumba' = the street
'¡Qué pena!' = What a pity; 'un trancón' = a police checkpoint; 'la rumba' = the line
questions.explanation: In Colombia, '¡Qué pena (con vos/usted)!' is the polite way to say 'I'm so sorry / excuse me', 'un trancón' is a traffic jam, and 'la rumba' is a party/night out!
